claim_edits.new_text: First generative interactive environment: 11B-parameter model trained on unlabelled Internet video: spatiotemporal tokenizer + autoregressive dynamics + scalable latent-action model enabling frame-by-frame action control without ground-truth action labels; latent actions train agents by imitation from unseen videos — a foundation-world-model claim.
claim_edits.old_text: First generative interactive environment from unlabelled Internet video at 11B scale: spatiotemporal tokenizer + autoregressive dynamics + scalable latent-action model enabling frame-by-frame action control without ground-truth action labels; latent actions train agents by imitation from unseen videos — a foundation-world-model claim.

new_claims.context: arXiv:2511.21631v2 §2 Model Architecture (Vision Encoder + MLP-based Vision-Language Merger) + §2.2 DeepStack + Fig.1 + §3.2.4 grounding coordinates.
new_claims.text: Vision-to-LLM projection uses a two-layer MLP merger compressing 2x2 visual features into one visual token matched to the LLM hidden size; DeepStack adds dedicated merger modules projecting features from three ViT levels into visual tokens added via residual connections to the first three LLM layers with no extra context length. The vision encoder is SigLIP-2 (SO-400M default; Large-300M for 2B/4B) with dynamic native-resolution input, 2D-RoPE and size-interpolated absolute embeddings; grounding coordinates are normalized to [0,1000].

Video time is encoded as explicit textual timestamp tokens prefixing each temporal patch (e.g. <3.0 seconds>); training uses both seconds and HMS (hours:minutes:seconds) formats so the model reads diverse timecodes. This replaces Qwen2.5-VL absolute-time positional alignment, avoiding large sparse temporal position IDs on long video and heavy uniform multi-fps sampling, at the cost of a modest context-length increase; it targets video grounding and dense captioning.

new_claims.context: arXiv:2511.21631v2 §3.1 Training Recipe + Table 1 (S0-S3 budgets/lengths) + Intro square-root loss note.
new_claims.text: Pre-training runs four stages: S0 trains only the merger on ~67B tokens at 8,192 length with encoder and LLM frozen; S1 full-parameter joint training on ~1T tokens at 8,192; S2 long-context training on ~1T tokens at 32,768 with more video/agent data; S3 ultra-long adaptation on 100B tokens at 262,144 focused on long video/document tasks. Text-only data is mixed throughout to preserve language ability; per-token square-root-normalized loss balances text and multimodal contributions.

new_claims.context: arXiv:2509.17765v1 §2.2 Audio Transformer (AuT) + Fig.3 + §2.3 input paragraph + §3-S1 Encoder Alignment.
new_claims.text: Audio input is resampled to 16 kHz into 128-channel mel-spectrograms (25 ms window, 10 ms hop) feeding the from-scratch AuT attention encoder-decoder (~0.6B params) trained on 20M hours of supervised audio (80% Chinese/English pseudo-labeled ASR, 10% other-language ASR, 10% audio understanding); Conv2D blocks downsample 8x to a 12.5 Hz token rate (~80 ms per frame), with flash attention over 1-8 s dynamic windows. Pretraining stage S1 trains the audio/vision adapters first on a fixed LLM, then the encoders.

new_claims.context: arXiv:2509.17765v1 §2.3 Video and Multimodal Position Embedding (TM-RoPE).
new_claims.text: TM-RoPE factorizes rotary embeddings into temporal/height/width with 24/20/20 interleaved angles (vs M-RoPE first-16 temporal angles): one temporal ID per 80 ms of audio, video frames stamped by actual timestamps at the same 80 ms granularity, and contiguous numbering across modalities (each modality starts at prior max + 1). Text uses identical triple IDs (=1D RoPE); images hold temporal ID constant. Unlike Qwen2.5-Omni fixed 2-second chunking, alignment is direct absolute-time ID matching, supporting arbitrary-duration streaming input with dynamic video frame rate.

new_claims.context: arXiv:2509.17765v1 §2.5 Designs for Streaming and Concurrency + Table 1 (module/params/streaming) + Table 2 (theoretical first-packet latency per concurrency).
new_claims.text: Streaming stack: chunked prefill with async Thinker-to-Talker handoff; MoE Thinker (30B-A3B) and Talker (3B-A0.3B) with MTP (80M) residual codebooks and causal-ConvNet Code2Wav (200M) synthesizing from the first 12.5 Hz codec frame (80 ms audio/token). Theoretical cold-start end-to-end first-packet latency at concurrency 1 is 234 ms audio / 547 ms video (tail 72/160 + Thinker TTFT 88/160 + Talker 57/210 + MTP 14 + decoder 3 ms); streaming RTF stays below 1 across concurrency 1/4/6. Author-calculated theory on vLLM with torch.compile/CUDA-Graph acceleration, not a measured deployment value; MoE KV-cache saving is qualitative only.

Architecture follows ViT-MLP-LLM: InternViT-300M (1B-14B models) or InternViT-6B (38B/78B) with Qwen2.5 (0.5B-72B) or InternLM3-8B bases (no instruction-tuned initialization), joined by a randomly initialized two-layer MLP projector; pixel-unshuffle cuts visual tokens to one quarter so each 448x448 tile yields 256 tokens, with dynamic-resolution tiling extended to multi-image and video.

new_claims.context: arXiv:2504.10479v3 §2.1 Variable Visual Position Encoding, Eqs.(1)-(4).
new_claims.text: V2PE assigns position indices recursively with +1 per text token but +δ<1 per visual token (Eqs.1-3); during training δ is sampled per image (held constant within an image) from {1,1/2,...,1/256} (Eq.4), and chosen at inference by sequence length to stay inside the context window; δ=1 reverts to standard encoding. Visual tokens thus spend less positional budget, extending multimodal context without dropping tokens (unlike pooling compression).

SFT grows 16.3M→21.7M samples (tools/3D/GUI/long-context/video/diagrams/CoT added) retaining random JPEG compression, square-loss reweighting and multimodal packing; MPO trains all models on ~300K pairs with weighted preference/quality/generation losses (Eq.9); test-time Best-of-N uses the VisualPRM-8B critic; the extended InternEVO framework (data/tensor/sequence/pipeline parallelism, dynamic visual-language load balancing, head+sequence parallel) supports sequences up to 32K tokens.

Images use one downscaled global crop plus up to K overlapping tiling crops (K=8 training, K=24 inference; untilable images downscaled); SFT uses 24 crops for 30% of pointing-annotated images. Video frames are single crops sampled at S=2 fps up to F=128 frames (F=384 long-context training), with uniform F-frame sampling beyond F/S seconds and the last frame always included; video pointing trains on examples with up to 60 annotated points.

The connector fuses third-to-last and ninth-from-last ViT layers: 2x2 patch windows for images (3x3 for video frames to cut tokens) pooled by multi-head attention using window means as queries, with shared image/video parameters and a shared MLP projection. The LLM receives visual tokens interleaved with text timestamps (video) or image indices (multi-image), column tokens for multi-crop aspect ratio (omitted for square single-crop), image/frame start tokens, and subtitles as timestamped text; vision tokens forward-attend across frames/images.

new_claims.context: arXiv:2601.10611v4 §3.2 Training (three-stage; 30k/bs128/16384; 2k/36864/F=384/CPx8/Ulysses) + Fig.3 packing/mask + Abstract recipe sentence.
new_claims.text: Three stages: lightweight image-only pre-training, joint video/image SFT (30k steps, batch 128, max length 16,384), then short long-context SFT on the same mixture (2k steps, length 36,864, F=384) with 8-GPU context-parallel groups (Ulysses attention) distributing ViT/pooling work. Packing jointly packs ViT crops and LLM tokens with message-tree encoding and masking (blocking cross-example and cross-QA attention); bidirectional attention over vision tokens and a token-weighting strategy add report-stated gains.
